related.why: Chest drain insertion: the treatment if the line causes a pneumothorax
Blood gases, including telling venous from arterial samples

brief.role: Core surgical trainee on the ICU rotation
brief.scenario: Mr Lewis Hensall, 68, is in septic shock from an anastomotic leak after an anterior resection, and needs noradrenaline. He is sedated and ventilated. Platelets 180 × 10⁹/L, INR 1.1. His last prophylactic dalteparin was 10 hours ago. The ICU registrar will supervise you inserting a right internal jugular central venous catheter.
brief.task: Talk the examiner through how you would insert the catheter, confirm its position and manage complications.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Checklist, full asepsis, real-time ultrasound, venous confirmation before dilating, wire out, then tip and lung checked.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating a venous-looking flashback or manometry as proof of tip position.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'd start with a checklist and time-out, and a scout scan of both necks."

grid.label: Checks, consent and safety standard
grid.fail: Starts without checking indication, bloods or consent status.
grid.pass: Indication, platelets and clotting, anticoagulant timing; best-interests decision as he is sedated; LocSSIP checklist and time-out.
grid.high: Knows prophylactic dalteparin need not be stopped; scout scans both internal jugular veins for patency and size first.

grid.label: Asepsis
grid.fail: Uses sterile gloves only, or doesn't let the skin preparation dry.
grid.pass: Maximal sterile barriers: cap, mask, sterile gown, sterile gloves, full-body drape; chlorhexidine in alcohol, allowed to dry.
grid.high: Sterile probe cover and sterile gel; knows the femoral vein carries higher infection and thrombosis risk in adults.

grid.label: Real-time ultrasound technique
grid.fail: Uses the landmark technique by choice, or scans only to mark the skin.
grid.pass: Real-time 2D ultrasound; head-down tilt; identifies vein and carotid; follows the needle tip into the vein.
grid.high: Scans proximally to confirm the wire stays in the vein and has not crossed another vessel before dilating.

grid.label: NICE TA49
grid.fail: Says ultrasound is optional, or that Doppler is recommended.
grid.pass: 2D ultrasound is the preferred method for elective internal jugular CVCs in adults and children; operators need training.
grid.high: Also: consider it in most circumstances, including emergencies; audio-guided Doppler not recommended.

grid.label: Wire control and venous confirmation
grid.fail: Dilates without confirming the wire is venous, or lets go of the wire.
grid.pass: Keeps hold of the wire; confirms venous placement (ultrasound, pressure transduction) before dilating; confirms wire removal.
grid.high: A 6 Fr or larger dilator or line in an artery: leave it, call vascular or interventional radiology. Retained wire: a Never Event.

grid.label: Complications
grid.fail: Names only infection, or can't name any.
grid.pass: Arterial puncture, haematoma, pneumothorax, air embolism, arrhythmia, malposition; later infection and thrombosis.
grid.high: Groups them as immediate and late; prevents air embolism with head-down tilt and closed hubs.

grid.label: Tip position and aftercare
grid.fail: Says manometry confirms the tip is in the right place; uses the line straight away.
grid.pass: Chest X-ray for tip position and pneumothorax before routine use; tip in lower SVC or at the cavo-atrial junction.
grid.high: Cavo-atrial junction lies about 4 cm (two vertebral bodies) below the carina; secures, dresses and documents the line.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd get the kit and put gloves on. He's sedated, so consent isn't needed.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How do you find the vein?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Landmarks: between the heads of sternocleidomastoid, aiming for the nipple. Ultrasound is optional.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Pass the wire, dilate and railroad the line.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How do you know it's in the right place?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Manometry shows it's venous, so the position is fine and the nurses can start the noradrenaline.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Check the indication, his platelets, clotting and anticoagulants. He lacks capacity, so a best-interests decision, and a LocSSIP checklist with time-out.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Cap, mask, sterile gown and gloves, full-body drape, and chlorhexidine in alcohol left to dry.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do you find the vein?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Real-time ultrasound with head-down tilt. I identify the vein and carotid and follow the needle tip into the vein. NICE TA49 recommends 2D ultrasound as the preferred method for elective internal jugular lines, by trained operators.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I pass the wire and keep hold of it, confirm it's venous on ultrasound or by pressure transduction, then dilate, and confirm the wire is out.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Arterial puncture, haematoma, pneumothorax, air embolism, arrhythmia, malposition, and later infection and thrombosis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Chest X-ray for the tip and a pneumothorax; tip in the lower SVC or at the cavo-atrial junction.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Checklist and time-out. Prophylactic dalteparin doesn't need stopping. I'd scout-scan both internal jugular veins for patency and size first.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Full barriers, a sterile probe cover and gel. I'd avoid the femoral vein: more infection and thrombosis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: TA49: 2D ultrasound preferred for elective internal jugular lines, considered in most circumstances including emergencies, operators trained, and audio-guided Doppler not recommended.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I scan up the vein to confirm the wire stays in it and hasn't crossed the carotid before dilating. If I'd put a 6 French dilator in the carotid, I'd leave it and call vascular or interventional radiology. Wire out, called aloud, witnessed; a retained wire is a Never Event.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Immediate: arterial puncture, pneumothorax, air embolism, arrhythmia. Late: infection, thrombosis. Head-down tilt and closed hubs prevent air embolism.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The cavo-atrial junction is about 4 centimetres, two vertebral bodies, below the carina; I'd check for pneumothorax, then secure, dress and document.

failures.move: Dilating before confirming the wire is venous.
failures.consequence: A large dilator in the carotid: haemorrhage, stroke or an emergency vascular repair.

failures.move: Accepting manometry as confirmation of tip position.
failures.consequence: Manometry shows the line is venous, not where the tip lies; a misplaced tip or pneumothorax goes unseen.

failures.move: Choosing the landmark technique for an elective internal jugular line.
failures.consequence: Higher risk of arterial puncture and failed attempts.

failures.move: Gloves only, or wiping off wet chlorhexidine.
failures.consequence: Higher risk of a catheter-related bloodstream infection in a patient already septic.

recovery.line: To be precise: it confirms the line is venous. The tip position needs a chest X-ray.

recovery.when: Pulsatile bright blood through the needle
recovery.line: I'd withdraw the needle, apply pressure and reassess with ultrasound, and tell my supervisor.

knowledge.fact: TA49: 2D ultrasound preferred for elective internal jugular CVCs in adults and children; consider in most circumstances; training required; audio-guided Doppler not recommended.
Real-time ultrasound for all central access; confirm the wire stays in the vein before dilating.
Inadvertent arterial line or dilator of 6 Fr or more: leave in place and discuss urgently with interventional radiology or vascular surgery.
Upper-body tip: lower third of SVC, cavo-atrial junction or high right atrium.
Maximal sterile barriers; more than 0.5% chlorhexidine in alcohol; avoid femoral access in adults.

recall.think: Carotid dilation, pneumothorax, air embolism, lost wire.
recall.say: "Real-time ultrasound, venous confirmation before dilating, chest X-ray for the tip."
do: Wire out; chest X-ray before use

numbers.meaning: in an artery: leave it and call for help

recall.trap: Venous blood or waveform does not show where the tip is.
recall.finish: Tip and lung checked on X-ray, line secured and documented, then vasopressor.

partner.opening: Mr Hensall is sedated and ventilated on noradrenaline through a peripheral cannula. Talk me through inserting a right internal jugular line.

reveals.trigger: Asks for bloods and drug chart
reveals.finding: Platelets 180 × 10⁹/L, INR 1.1, dalteparin 5000 units 10 hours ago.
Right internal jugular vein patent, compressible, lateral to the carotid.

reveals.trigger: Asks to confirm the wire is venous
reveals.finding: Ultrasound shows the wire in the vein along its length.
Tip about 4 cm below the carina; no pneumothorax.

push.question: What checks before you start?
push.expect: Indication, clotting, anticoagulants, best interests, LocSSIP time-out.

push.question: How do you prevent infection?
push.expect: Maximal sterile barriers; chlorhexidine in alcohol, dry.

push.question: What does NICE TA49 say?
push.expect: 2D ultrasound preferred for elective IJV lines; consider in most cases; training; no audio Doppler.

push.question: What complications do you warn about?
push.expect: Arterial puncture, pneumothorax, air embolism, arrhythmia, malposition, infection, thrombosis.

push.question: How do you confirm position?
push.expect: Chest X-ray for tip and pneumothorax, not manometry.

curveballs.prompt: The transduced trace from the line is pulsatile at 110/60.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Arterial placement: don't remove a large-bore line; leave it, don't use it, call vascular or interventional radiology.

curveballs.prompt: After dilating, his SpO2 falls and airway pressures rise.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Suspect pneumothorax; examine, ultrasound or X-ray, and decompress with a chest drain; tell the supervisor.

curveballs.prompt: At the end, the wire can't be found on the tray.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop and account for it; chest X-ray to look for a retained wire; tell the supervisor and report it.

curveballs.prompt: The chest X-ray shows the tip in the right internal jugular heading up the neck.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Malposition: don't use it for vasopressor; reposition or replace under supervision.
